CONFIRMATION QUESTIONS
• Three categories
- DRG global challenges, USAID DRG efforts within USG's DRG
efforts, questions related to previous administration
• USAID engaged in programmatic areas related to the questions
• Further programmatic context that provides additional background
for questions

USAID DRG OVERVIEW
• Contributes to establish and consolidate inclusive and accountable
democracies to advance freedom, dignity, and development
• 80 USAID Missions that program DRG funds globally: 66% in closing
space
• Approximately 600 DRG global cadre members
• Thematic Areas: Governance, Anti-Corruption, Human Rights,
Resurgent Authoritarianism, Rule of Law, Civil Society, Media, Labor,
Cross-Sectoral Programs, Elections and Political Processes
• Impact of USAID democracy assistance
• $2.4 billion democracy directive since 2016
- of which, approximately $1.6 billion is managed by USAID
- of which, $130 million is managed by DRG Center

OTHER U.S. DRG ASSISTANCE ACTORS
• National Endowment for Democracy (NED)
- $300 million annual budget, separate from the $2.4 billion directive
• Dept of State, Bureau for International Narcotics and Law
Enforcement (INL)
- $350 million DRG budget; overlap in Rule of Law and Anti-Corruption areas
• Dept of State, Bureau for Democracy, Human Rights and
Labor (DRL)
- $225 million budget; more than doubled in past 5 years; overlap in Civil Society,
Media, Labor, and Human Rights

COUNTERING RESURGENT
AUTHORITARIANISM/CHINA
USAID Role
• Make it a priority
• Pivot from Clear Choice to countering resurgent authoritarianism
Approach
• Doing development democratically
• Combat corruption and elite capture, strengthen institutional
resilience
• Counter digital authoritarianism and disinformation
Emerging Issue
• Opportunity: $300M Countering Chinese Influence Fund (CCIF)-
operationalization of countering Resurgent Authoritarian Influence

COVID AND DRG
USAID's Role
• Rapid Program Adaptations
Approach
• Technical Guidance to the Field
• Responsive, Timely, and Flexible Funding
• Coordination with internal and external stakeholders
Emerging Issues
• Priority and urgency of 'integration' across all sectors
• Technical Learning
• Adaptive approaches to enhance responsiveness

GOVERNANCE and ANTI-CORRUPTION
USAID Role
• Leading USG and donor agency in governance and anti-corruption
• Ensure governance is integrated across sectors to enable countries
to achieve SDG outcomes
Approach
• Build more effective, responsive and accountable institutions
• Enhance capacity to mobilize and use resources to meet public needs
• Strengthen ecosystem for combating corruption
Emerging Issues
• Debt accumulation, Debt traps
• Pervasive corruption, as illustrated by COVID-19 response
10

CIVIL SOCIETY/CIVIC SPACE
USAID Role:
• Lead donor
• Closing spaces - prevention, adaptation
• Youth and civic engagement
Approach:
• New program approaches
• Global, Regional & Bilateral programming
Emerging Issues:
11

INDEPENDENT MEDIA AND FREEDOM OF
EXPRESSION
USAID Role
• One of largest donors for independent media development
Approach
• Independent media development
- Newsroom professionalization and journalism quality
- Media literacy and social participation in media
- Legal and regulatory enabling conditions
- Financial viability of the sector/digital innovation
- Journalist safety
• Internet freedom programming
Emerging Issues
• Disinformation
12

JUSTICE AND HUMAN RIGHTS
USAID Role:
• Leadership in building accountability
Approach:
• Rule of Law: opportunity to re-elevate the sector. Supporting full
spectrum of justice chain
• Human rights: environment building, response, and remedy.
• Atrocity Prevention: prevention, response and recovery
• Security Sector Reform: building internal accountability
Emerging Issues:
• Challenges - declining budgets, need for more responsive
programming
• Opportunities to re-elevate the sector
13

COUNTERING TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS
USAID Role
• Since 200l: $340M spent in 88 countries and regions
• C-TIP Directive: $22M/yr attribution; spend $30-$35M
• Strong interagency coordination
Approach
• Four P's approach (prevention, protection, prosecution,
partnerships)
• USAID's comparative advantage
Emerging Issues
• DOS TIP Report and Tier 3 waivers
• Revised Policy: emphasis on survivor and trauma-information
approach; evidence and data driven
14

LABOR
USAID Role
• Long-standing Congressional Directive plus bilateral programming
• Strong interagency coordination
Approach
• Partnership with Solidarity Center
• Fully invested in the value of unions and worker associations
• Two-pronged approach to managing the Global Labor Directive
Emerging Issues
• COVID-19 and closing space in the world of work
15

ELECTIONS AND POLITICAL PROCESSES
USAID Role
• Leader in Elections and Political Processes Field
• "Go to" in Interagency
Approach
• Technical leadership and guidance
• Field-driven programming
• Key partners
Emerging Issues
• Electoral technologies and cybersecurity
• Countering malign influence
• Participation and inclusion
16
